subject: TEST-NUMVAL-F function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: `cite.py --check 15.95.2 "FUNCTION"` -> OK, printing the format verbatim: `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-NUMVAL-F</u> ( argument-1 )` (General format). The format is FUNCTION + the name + a parenthesized list of EXACTLY ONE argument; nothing is bracketed, so both the argument and its parens are required and no second argument is admitted. CODE READ (not sampled): (1) the reference shape comes from the ONE generic rule `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` in src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 — TEST-NUMVAL-F is not a reserved word (it is not in the four-word §8.9 n §8.11 set SIGN/SUM/LENGTH/RANDOM), so it arrives through `functionName` and the FNARG_LPAREN retyping makes the '(' the argument list per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6; (2) the ARITY is the catalog row's, `Add(new("TEST-NUMVAL-F", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "TestNumvalF", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002))` inside IntrinsicCatalog.Build; (3) it is ENFORCED at IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore — `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` raises COBOL1504 "FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)". I traced both degenerate shapes to that arm rather than assuming them: a BARE `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F` (no parens) reaches `FinishIntrinsic(fc, BindIntrinsicCore(name, ArgsOf(fc.functionArgList())), display)` at IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsic:89 with an EMPTY list (the paren group is optional in the grammar), so given=0 < MinArgs=1 -> COBOL1504; a two-argument write gives 2 > MaxArgs=1 -> COBOL1504. The MinArgs!=0 guards at IntrinsicBinder:301/339 belong to the KEYWORD-OMITTED (§8.4.3.2.3 SR2) route and cannot swallow the FUNCTION-keyword form. (4) The NAME resolves — the catalog row exists, so COBOL1501 ("not an intrinsic function of ISO/IEC 1989") does not fire, and the edition window is applied by IntrinsicBinder:493 (COBOL1502 below the introduction edition). TESTS: `tests/conformance/2023/pb60_numval_one_scan.cob` writes `COMPUTE T = FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F("1 2")` and its .out pins `ET=000C` (the overpunched +3), and IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.TestNumvalF_Positions_2014 exercises the same one-argument form four more times through AssertSpec (which compares against a HARDCODED spec-derived expectation, not against the legacy oracle or GnuCOBOL — I read the helper at line 26 to confirm that before citing it). EDITIONS: taken from kb/Work R28 (landed), whose evidence is EXTERNAL to this code — the COBOL Consortium's COBOL2002 introduction names NUMVAL-F/TEST-NUMVAL-F among the functions added by COBOL2002, and both are absent from the WG4 2014-cycle new-function lists; the 2023 text itself cannot settle it (Annex E fixes only the 2014->2023 boundary and §8.11 lists names with no edition data). I did NOT derive the window from IntrinsicCatalog's own row. REFUTED: VERDICT SURVIVES (CONFORMS); one qualifying spec-derived test the adjudicator missed is ADDED to test-ref. I did not accept the adjudicator's trace — the citation was re-derived by me (`cite.py --check 15.95.2 "TEST-NUMVAL-F"` -> OK, §15.95.2 General format, `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-NUMVAL-F</u> ( argument-1 )`) and the row was attacked on four axes. (1) ARITY, read from the source rather than from the note: IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore computes `long given = args.Sum(a => a is BoundFieldOperand { Place: TableAllPlace all } ? all.StaticCount ?? 1 : 1)` and `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` raises COBOL1504 BEFORE CheckArgumentClasses; the catalog row supplies MinArgs=MaxArgs=1. The BARE form resolves the same way for a reason the adjudicator did not state: the SR6 guard `fc.FNARG_LPAREN() is null && fc.refModPart().Length != 0` is FALSE for a bare name (no refModPart), so control falls to FinishIntrinsic over a null functionArgList -> given=0 -> COBOL1504. (2) THE EDGE THE ADJUDICATOR DID NOT NAME, AND IT HOLDS: the format shows NO reference modification and §15.95.1 makes the type INTEGER, so `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F(x)(1:2)` must be refused — it reaches FinishIntrinsic -> ResultRefMod, whose §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 arm admits only PicCategory Alphanumeric/National/Boolean and otherwise reports DiagnosticCatalog.RefModFunctionResultClass; and the argument-less `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F (1:2)` is caught one step earlier by DefinitionPermitsArguments -> Sr6ArgumentListError (COBOL1543, §8.4.3.2.3 SR6). (3) THE TWO-ARM CHECK, run independently because that shape has recurred five times here: I read RenderDec myself — its `alwaysDec` list is Annuity/PresentValue/Variance/StandardDeviation/Numval/NumvalC/NumvalF/Sum/Range/Mean/Median/Midrange and does NOT contain TestNumvalF, its switch ends `_ => null`, and a string argument makes `AnyDecOrRealRaw` false — so under `num.StandardDecimal` RenderDec returns null and RenderNum's `case "TestNumvalF"` is the ONLY emitter arm. I also grepped the whole compiler for a compile-time folder (ConstFold/ConstantFold/TryFold/FoldIntrinsic): there is none, so there is genuinely one body, not two. (4) EDITIONS: I opened kb/Work/R28.md rather than trusting the summary of it — its evidence is the COBOL Consortium's COBOL2002 introduction plus the WG4/J4 CD 1.2 (2009-08-23) Annex D.2 new-function list, both EXTERNAL to IntrinsicCatalog, and R28 records that the 2023 PDF's §15.6 Table 21 cannot settle the 2002 boundary at all. 2002,2014,2023 stands and is not catalog-derived. TEST-REF EXTENDED: tests/conformance/2014/formatted_datetime.cob:54 writes `MOVE FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F("0 1E+2") TO WS-N` and its .out pins `TNF=+000000003` — a spec-derived golden exercising this exact one-argument format at edition 2014, which the adjudicator did not cite.
